compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The daily worktree GC (`~/.local/bin/rebar-worktree-gc.sh`, LaunchAgent
`com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc`, 04:00 daily) **hangs indefinitely** on a single
`git status --porcelain`, and because it takes an atomic-mkdir single-flight lock BEFORE that
point, every subsequent scheduled run exits via `SKIP: another gc run in progress`. The GC had
therefore not completed since **Sep 4**, and 173 worktrees (~111 GB) accumulated.

## Observed 2026-09-05

```
PID 75958  PPID 1  STAT S  ELAPSED 12:08:32  %CPU 0.0
  /bin/bash ~/.local/bin/rebar-worktree-gc.sh --apply
child 50208  STAT S  ELAPSED 11:59:18  %CPU 0.0

blocked on:  git status --porcelain  in /Users/joeoakhart/janitor-1a63-docs
lock held:   ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/worktree-gc.lock   (mkdir Sep 5 04:00)
last-run:    1788519781  (Sep 4)
```

0.0% CPU for twelve hours — blocked, not computing. Host disk was measured at **30k tps /
150 MB/s** during the same window, so the cause is host-wide IO saturation rather than anything
specific to that worktree. The GC processes worktrees alphabetically, reaches the `janitor-*`
block, and dies there nightly.

## Defect 1 — an unbounded `git status` inside a lock

`git status --porcelain` has no timeout. Under IO pressure it can block forever, and it does so
while holding the single-flight lock, which converts a transient stall into a PERMANENT outage of
the whole GC.

**Suggested direction:** bound the per-worktree `git status` and treat a timeout as
**"unknown -> KEEP"**, which is the safe direction — a worktree wrongly kept costs disk, one
wrongly removed can cost unlanded work. Note `timeout` does not exist on macOS; use the
`perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'` form documented in AGENTS.md.

## Defect 2 — the stale lock outlives the process

The lock is `mkdir "$LOCK"` (line 71). Killing the hung process does **not** release it: the
directory persists and every future run SKIPs forever. Verified today — after killing PID 75958 the
lock directory was still present and empty; it had to be removed by hand before acquisition
succeeded.

**Suggested direction:** record the holder PID in the lock and treat a lock whose holder is dead as
stale (acquire and log it), or clean up on EXIT/TERM. A single-flight guard that cannot distinguish
"a run is in progress" from "a run died three days ago" is a check that stops checking.

## Defect 3 — `.rebar/usage.jsonl` is a false ACTIVE signal

The idle test treats a worktree as active if any file changed within 24h. **17 of 50** worktrees
kept as "active" were held back SOLELY because rebar's own telemetry file `.rebar/usage.jsonl` was
written recently; 3 more by `src/rebar/_build_info.py`. Neither indicates human or agent work — they
are the tool observing itself.

Adding both to the GC's `NOISE_RE` would unlock roughly **20 further removals (~13 GB)** on the next
run. Confirm the count before and after rather than trusting this estimate.

## Why it went unnoticed — the diagnostic surface is misleading

`launchctl list` renders a running job as:

```
75958	0	com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc
```

The first column is the PID **when running** and the second is the LAST EXIT STATUS. A reader
(including this orchestrator, earlier today) can easily read `0` as "last run exited cleanly" and
conclude the job is healthy — when the presence of a PID means it is running RIGHT NOW, and in this
case had been for twelve hours. Compounding it, the run's log file contains a normal-looking
sequence of `KEEP`/`REMOVED` lines, because it wedged partway through rather than at the start.

The reliable signals are the `last-run` stamp and the elapsed time of the PID, not the exit column.

## Interim actions already taken (2026-09-05)

- Killed PID 75958 (TERM, then KILL — it did not exit on TERM) and its child 50208.
- Removed the stale lock directory by hand and verified acquisition with the script's own
  `mkdir` mechanism.
- A one-off manual GC pass removed **61 worktrees / 38.7 GiB** (173 -> 113), creating 101
  `refs/salvage/<branch>` refs first so every removal is reversible, and using
  `git worktree remove` WITHOUT `--force` so git independently refused on any dirt (0 refusals).

So tonight's backlog is cleared, but the defects remain and the GC will hang again on the next
IO-saturated night.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 A blocked `git status` cannot hang the GC indefinitely; a timeout is treated as
      "unknown -> keep" and logged.
- [ ] AC2 A lock whose holder is dead is detected as stale and does not permanently disable the GC.
      Prove both branches: a live holder still blocks, a dead holder does not.
- [ ] AC3 `.rebar/usage.jsonl` and `src/rebar/_build_info.py` no longer count as activity;
      report the before/after kept-active count on a real run.
- [ ] AC4 A stalled or non-completing GC is DETECTABLE without reading `ps` — e.g. the `last-run`
      stamp age is surfaced somewhere a human or agent will see it.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. `timeout` does not exist on this macOS host (exit 127) —
bound with `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'`. Do not touch the shared main checkout; do not
`git stash` anywhere.
compiled_state.title: Worktree GC hangs on an unbounded git status inside its lock, silently disabling itself for days
